newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed, liquidity ample.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed, liquidity ample.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in dull late trading on Wednesday.
Dealers said money market liquidity turned ample late in the afternoon, with overnight money falling to nine percent, but the rupiah remained firm against the dollar.
One local bank dealer said speculation for a higher central bank fixing did not materialise, causing operators to unload dollars they had bought earlier.
Spot rupiah edged up to 2,371.30/71.75 at 0915 GMT from an earlier low of 2,372.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,371.0/71.5 and 2,370.0/70.6, respectively.
Dealers said short-term swaps fell following an easing in the money market. Tom/next swap fell to 0.3/0.4 from 0.5.
Overnight swap was last at 0.50/0.55 points.
Longer-term swaps were relatively stable, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said unstable short-term swap rates prevented operators to go long on dollars.
"We are still reluctant to take up long positions because we could be forced to cut losses with volatile short-term swaps, while potential gains are marginal," he said.
"We rather wait and see how things develop," he added.
One-month swaps were at 11.25/11.75, two at 22.00/23.00, three at 34.00/35.00 and six at 71.75/72.25 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,368.0/2.560 and the conversion band at 2,368/2,416 on Wednesday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by four points last week and by only one point so far this week.
